<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{heatkerneltheorem}

Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph satisfying sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates HK($\beta$). Let $W$ be a graph potential in the Kato class $K^\infty(V, \mu)$. If $\Delta_\mu+W$ is subcritical, then there exist constants $c_1, c_2, c_3, c_4>0$ such that for all $x,y\in V$ and all $n\geq d(x,y)$, $$\frac{c_1}{V_\mu(x,n^{1/\beta})}\exp\left(-c_2\left(\frac{d(x,y)^\beta}{n}\right)^{1/(\beta-1)}\right)\leq p_\mu^W(x,y,n)\leq \frac{c_3}{V_\mu(x,n^{1/\beta})}\exp\left(-c_4\left(\frac{d(x,y)^\beta}{n}\right)^{1/(\beta-1)}\right).$$
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
A \textbf{weighted graph} is a pair $(V, \mu)$ where $V$ is a set and $\mu \colon V\cup V^2 \rightarrow [0, \infty)$ is a function such that $\mu(x)>0$ for all $x\in V$, $\mu(x,y)=\mu(y,x)$ for all pairs $(x,y)\in V^2$ and for each $x\in V$, $\sum_{y\in V} \mu(x,y)= \mu(x).$
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
Let $\Omega\subseteq V$.

\noindent (i) A \textbf{path} in $\Omega$ is a sequence $x_0, \dots, x_N\in \Omega$ with $x_j\sim x_{j+1}$ for $j=0, \dots, N-1$. Given such a path, we define $N$ to be its \textbf{length}.\\

\noindent (ii) $\Omega$ is \textbf{connected} if for any $x,y\in \Omega$ there is a path $x_0, \dots, x_N$ with $x_0=x$ and $x_N=y$.\\

\noindent (iii) The (exterior) \textbf{boundary} of $\Omega$ is the set $$\partial \Omega=\left\{x\notin \Omega\colon x\sim y \textrm{ for some }y\in \Omega\right\}.$$
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph. The \textbf{distance} $d(x,y)$ between $x,y\in V$ is the length of the shortest path from $x$ to $y$. If there is no such path we say $d(x,y)=+\infty$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph. The \textbf{Markov kernel} of $(V, \mu)$ is the function \begin{equation}K_\mu(x,y)=\frac{\mu_{xy}}{\mu(x)}.\end{equation} Given $f \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$ we define \begin{equation}(K_\mu f)(x)=\sum_{y\in V} K_\mu(x,y)f(y).\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
We say that the weighted graph $(V, \mu)$ has \textbf{controlled weights} if there exists $C>1$ such that for all $x\in V$ and $x\sim y$ we have \begin{equation} \frac{\mu_{xy}}{\mu(x)}\geq \frac{1}{C}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
We call the weighted graph $(V, \mu)$ \textbf{uniformly lazy} if there exists $c>0$ with $K_\mu(x,x)\geq c$ for all $x\in V$.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph. The \textbf{heat kernel} of $(V, \mu)$ is given for $x,y\in V$ and $n\in \mathbf{N}$ as \begin{equation}p_\mu(x,y,n)=\frac{K_{n,\mu}(x,y)}{\mu(y)}.\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph. The \textbf{Laplacian} of $(V, \mu)$, denoted $\Delta_\mu$, is the operator $$\Delta_\mu=I-K_\mu$$ where $I$ is the identity.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
The \textbf{Green's function} of the weighted graph $(V,\mu)$ is defined by
\[ G_{\mu}(x,y) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty p_\mu(x,y,n).\]
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
The weighted graph $(V,\mu)$ is said to be \textbf{transient} if $G_\mu(x,y) < +\infty$ for all $(x,y) \in V \times V$ (in particular, this includes all pairs $(x,x)$). Otherwise, $(V, \mu)$ is said to be \textbf{recurrent}.
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
\label{hkbeta}
    Let $\beta\geq 2$. The weighted graph $(V, \mu)$ satisfies \textbf{sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates with exponent $\beta$}, abbreviated \textbf{HK($\beta$)}, provided there exist constants $c_1, c_2, c_3, c_4>0$ such that for all $x,y\in V$ and all $n\geq d(x,y)$, $$\frac{c_1}{V_\mu(x,n^{1/\beta})}\exp\left(-c_2\left(\frac{d(x,y)^\beta}{n}\right)^{1/(\beta-1)}\right)\leq p_\mu(x,y,n)\leq \frac{c_3}{V_\mu(x,n^{1/\beta})}\exp\left(-c_4\left(\frac{d(x,y)^\beta}{n}\right)^{1/(\beta-1)}\right).$$
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{bassbarlowthm} (Barlow-Bass \cite{barlowbass1}, Theorem 1.1)
    Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph and let $\nu$ be such that $\nu\asymp \mu$. Then $(V, \mu)$ satisfies HK($\beta$) if and only if $(V, \nu)$ does.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
Let $\beta\geq 2$ and $\alpha>0$. The weighted graph $(V, \mu)$ satisfies \textbf{HK$(\alpha, \beta)$} provided $(V, \mu)$ satisfies HK($\beta$) and also $V_\mu(x,r)\asymp r^\alpha$ over all $x\in V$ and all $r\geq 1$.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{greenest0}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph satisfying HK$(\beta)$. Then we have that $$G_\mu(x,y)\asymp \sum_{n=d(x,y)}^\infty \frac{n^{\beta-1}}{V_\mu(x,n)}.$$
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
The proof can be adapted with minimal changes from the proof of Proposition 4.2 in Delmotte \cite{delmotte1}, which proves the statement for $\beta=2$.\qed
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{greenest}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph satisfying HK$(\alpha,\beta)$. Then $\alpha>\beta$ and we have that $$G_\mu(x,y)\asymp \frac{1}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}.$$
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph and let $W \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$ be a real-valued function. The \textbf{Schr\"odinger operator associated to $W$} is the operator $\Delta_\mu+W$, where we view $W$ as a multiplication operator on functions on $V$.
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph and let $W \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$. A real-valued function $u$ is called a \textbf{profile for $(\Delta_\mu+W)$} if $u$ is defined on all of $V$, $u>0$, and $(\Delta_\mu+W)u=0$.
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
\label{graphpotentialdef}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph. A function $W \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$ is called a \textbf{graph potential on $(V, \mu)$} if there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that for all $x\in V$, \begin{equation} W(x)\leq K_\mu(x,x)-\epsilon.\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
\label{subcriticaldef}
    Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph and $W$ a graph potential on $(V, \mu)$. The Schr\"odinger operator $\Delta_\mu+W$ is called \textbf{subcritical} if the Green's function $G_\mu^W(x,y)$ exists, in other words if $$\sum_{n=0}^\infty p_\mu^W(x,y,n)<+\infty$$ for some (any) $x,y\in V$.
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph and let $W$ be a graph potential on $(V, \mu)$. There exists a constant $C=C(V, \mu)>0$ such that for any $u\geq 0$ with $$(\Delta_\mu+W)u(x)=0$$ we have $$u(y)\leq Cu(x)$$  for $y\sim x$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
From $$(\Delta_\mu+W)u(x)=0$$ we obtain $$u(x)+W(x)u(x)=K_\mu u$$ and therefore $$\big(1-K_\mu(x,x)+W(x)\big)u(x)=\sum_{y\sim x}K_\mu(x,y)u(y).$$ If $1-K_\mu(x,x)+W(x)=0$, this implies $u(y)=0$ for all $y\sim x$ and therefore any $C>0$ works. If $1-K_\mu(x,x)+W(x)<0$, we must have $u(x)=u(y)=0$ for all $y\sim x$ and therefore any $C>0$ works. Since $(V, \mu)$ has controlled weights, there exists $C_1>0$ such that $K_\mu(x,y)\geq 1/C_1$ for all $x\in V$ and all $y\sim x$. Also, we have that $1-K_\mu(x,x)+W(x)\leq 2$ since $W$ is a graph potential. Therefore, taking $$C=C(V, \mu)=2C_1$$ works, since $\big(1-K_\mu(x,x)+W(x)\big)u(x)=\sum_{y\sim x}K_\mu(x,y)u(y)$ implies $$K_\mu(x,y)u(y)\leq \big(1-K_\mu(x,x)+W(x)\big)u(x)\leq 2u(x)$$ and thus $u(y)\leq Cu(x)$.\qed
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
The proof above shows that existence of positive $u>0$ with $(\Delta_\mu+W)u=0$ on $V$ implies $1-K_\mu(x,x)+W(x)>0$ or $W(x)>K_\mu(x,x)-1$ for all $x\in V$.\\
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{localharnackfull}
Let $\Omega\subseteq V$ be finite and connected and let $W \colon \Omega \rightarrow \mathbf R$ be a graph potential. There exists $C=C(\Omega)>0$ such that for any $u\geq 0$ on $\Omega\cup\partial \Omega$ with $(\Delta_\mu+W)u=0$ on $\Omega$, we have $$\sup_\Omega u\leq C\inf_\Omega u.$$
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{harnackprinciple}
Let $\Omega\subseteq V$ be connected and let $W \colon \Omega \rightarrow \mathbf R$ be a graph potential. Let $(u_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a sequence of functions such that $u_n\geq 0$ on $\Omega\cup \partial \Omega$ and $(\Delta_\mu+W)u_n=0$ on $\Omega$. Then either $u_n\rightarrow +\infty$ pointwise on $\Omega$ or there exists $u\geq 0$ with $(\Delta_\mu+W)u=0$ on $\Omega$ and a subsequence $(u_{n_k})_{k\geq 0}$ of $(u_n)_{n \geq 0}$ such that $u_{n_k}\rightarrow u$ pointwise on $\Omega$.\qed
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph and let $\Delta_\mu+W$ be subcritical. Then there exists a profile for $\Delta_\mu+W$, i.e. a function $h>0$ satisfying $$(\Delta_\mu+W)h=0.$$
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- head-4: body_md -->
Let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in $V$ tending to infinity. Let $$h_n(x):= \frac{G_\mu^W(x, x_n)}{G_\mu^W(x_0, x_n)}.$$ Note that $h_n(x_0)=1$ for all $n\geq 0$ and $(\Delta_\mu+W)h_n=0$ on $V\setminus \left\{x_n\right\}$. By the Harnack principle Lemma \ref{harnackprinciple}, $(h_n)_{n\geq 0}$ has a pointwise convergent subsequence. The pointwise limit $h$ must be a profile for $\Delta_\mu+W$.\qed
<!-- end head-4 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
A weighted graph $(V, \mu)$ satisfies the \textbf{scale-invariant elliptic Harnack inequality (EHI)} if there exists a constant $C_H$ such that for any ball $B$ and any non-negative $\Delta_\mu$-harmonic function $u$ defined on $2B$, we have $$\sup_B u\leq C_H\inf_B u.$$
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{liouville}
(Liouville's Theorem) Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph satisfying (EHI). Let $u>0$ be a positive $\Delta_\mu$-harmonic function defined on all of $V$. Then $u$ is constant.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- head-5: body_md -->
Let $w=u-\inf_V u$. This function is harmonic and non-negative. We also have $\inf_V w=0$. Fix $x\in M$ and note that $$\sup_{B(x,r)} w\leq C_H \inf_{B(x,r)} w$$ for any $r>0$. Letting $r\rightarrow +\infty$ we see that $\sup_{V} w=0$. Hence $u$ is constant.\qed
<!-- end head-5 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph. A real-valued function $W$ on $V$ is \textbf{Green-bounded} on $(V, \mu)$ if $$\left\VertW\right\Vert_\mu:=\sup_{x\in V} \sum_{y\in V} \left\vertW(y)\right\vert G_\mu(x,y)\mu(y)<+\infty.$$
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
\label{katoinfinity}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph. For a real-valued function $W$ on $V,$ the \textbf{Kato infinity class} $K^\infty(V, \mu, \alpha)$ is defined as follows: $W\in K^\infty(V, \mu, \alpha)$ provided $$\lim_{R\rightarrow \infty} \sup_{x\in V} \sum_{y\in V\setminus B(o, R)} \left\vertW(y)\right\vert G_\mu(x,y)\mu(y)<\alpha.$$ We also define $$K^\infty(V, \mu)=\bigcap_{s>0} K^\infty(V, \mu, s).$$
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{katodecay}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph satisfying HK($\alpha$, $\beta$). Fix $o\in M$ and for $x\in V$ set $\left< x \right>=1+d(o, x)$. Assume that $W \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$ satisfies $\left\vertW(x)\right\vert\preceq \left< x \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}$ for some $\epsilon>0$. Then $W\in K^\infty(V, \mu)$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- head-6: body_md -->
Let $R>1$ and let $\Gamma=V\setminus B(o, R)$. Let $x\in V$. We have that $$\sum_{y\in \Gamma} G_\mu(x,y)\left\vertW(y)\right\vert\mu(y)\preceq \sum_{y\in \Gamma} \frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y).$$ For $y\in \Gamma$ such that $d(y, o)\geq 2 d(x, o)$ we have that $$d(x,y)\geq d(y,o)-d(x,o)\geq d(y,o)-\frac{1}{2}d(y,o)\succeq \left< y \right>.$$ 

Therefore for such $y\in \Gamma$ we have $$\frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\preceq \left< y \right>^{-(\alpha+\epsilon)}.$$

We then have that $$\sum_{y\in \Gamma} \frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y)=\sum_{y\in \Gamma\setminus B(o, 2\left< x \right>)} \frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y)+\sum_{y\in \Gamma\cap B(o, 2\left< x \right>)}\frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y)$$ $$\preceq \sum_{y\in \Gamma\setminus B(o, 2\left< x \right>)} \left< y \right>^{-(\alpha+\epsilon)}\mu(y)+\sum_{y\in \Gamma \cap B(o, 2\left< x \right>)}\frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y).$$ 

First, let $\mathfrak{L}\in \mathbf{N}$ be such that $2^{\mathfrak{L}}\leq R\leq 2^{\mathfrak{L}+1}$. We then have that $$\sum_{y\in \Gamma\setminus B(o, 2\left< x \right>)} \left< y \right>^{-(\alpha+\epsilon)}\mu(y)\leq \sum_{y\in \Gamma} \left< y \right>^{-(\alpha+\epsilon)}\mu(y)\preceq \sum_{n=\mathfrak{L}}^\infty \left(\sum_{y\in B(o, 2^{n+1})\setminus B(o, 2^n)}\left< y \right>^{-(\alpha+\epsilon)}\mu(y)\right)$$ $$\asymp \sum_{n=\mathfrak{L}}^\infty \left(\sum_{y\in B(o, 2^{n+1})\setminus B(o, 2^n)}(2^n)^{-(\alpha+\epsilon)}\mu(y)\right)\preceq \sum_{n=\mathfrak{L}}^\infty (2^n)^{-\epsilon}\preceq R^{-\epsilon}.$$

 Next, if $\left\vertx\right\vert\leq R/2$, then the next term is zero. Otherwise, $$\sum_{y\in \Gamma\cap B(o, 2\left< x \right>)}\frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y)=\sum_{y\in B(x, \frac{1}{2}\left< x \right>)}\frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y)+\sum_{y\in B(o, 2\left< x \right>)\setminus B(x, \frac{1}{2}\left< x \right>)}\frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y).$$ 

If $y\in B(x, \frac{1}{2}\left< x \right>)$, then $\left< y \right>\asymp \left< x \right>$. Letting $N\in \mathbf{N}$ with $2^N\leq \left< x \right>\leq 2^{N+1}$ we then have that $$\sum_{y\in B(x, \frac{1}{2}\left< x \right>)}\frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y)\asymp \sum_{y\in B(x, \frac{1}{2}\left< x \right>)}\frac{\left< x \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y)$$ $$\preceq \left< x \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}\sum_{n=0}^N \sum_{y\in B(x, 2^{n+1})\setminus B(x, 2^n)}\frac{\mu(y)}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}} \asymp \left< x \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}\sum_{n=0}^N \sum_{y\in B(x, 2^{n+1})\setminus B(x, 2^n)}\frac{\mu(y)}{(2^n)^{\alpha-\beta}}$$ $$\preceq\left< x \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}\sum_{n=0}^N \frac{(2^n)^\alpha}{(2^n)^{\alpha-\beta}}=\left< x \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}\sum_{n=0}^N (2^\beta)^n\asymp \left< x \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}(2^N)^\beta\asymp \left< x \right>^{-\epsilon}\preceq R^{-\epsilon}.$$

Finally, if $y\in B(o, 2\left< x \right>)\setminus B(x, \frac{1}{2}\left< x \right>)$, then $d(x,y)\asymp \left< x \right>$. Therefore letting $N$ be as before with $2^N\leq \left< x \right>\leq 2^{N+1}$, we have $$\sum_{y\in B(o, 2\left< x \right>)\setminus B(x, \frac{1}{2}\left< x \right>)}\frac{\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}}{d(x,y)^{\alpha-\beta}}\mu(y)\asymp \left< x \right>^{\beta-\alpha}\left(\sum_{y\in B(o, 2\left< x \right>)\setminus B(x, \frac{1}{2}\left< x \right>)}\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}\mu(y)\right)$$ $$\preceq \left< x \right>^{\beta-\alpha}\sum_{n=0}^N \left(\sum_{y\in B(o, 2^{n+1})\setminus B(o, 2^{n+1})}\left< y \right>^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}\mu(y)\right)\asymp \left< x \right>^{\beta-\alpha}\sum_{n=0}^N \left(\sum_{y\in B(o, 2^{n+1})\setminus B(o, 2^{n+1})}(2^n)^{-(\beta+\epsilon)}\mu(y)\right)$$ $$\preceq \left< x \right>^{\beta-\alpha}\sum_{n=0}^N (2^n)^{\alpha-(\beta+\epsilon)}$$ $$\asymp \left< x \right>^{\beta-\alpha}(2^N)^{\alpha-(\beta+\epsilon)}\asymp \left< x \right>^{-\epsilon}\preceq R^{-\epsilon}.$$

Putting all three pieces together, we find that $$\sum_{y\in V\setminus B(o, R)} G_\mu(x,y)\left\vertW(y)\right\vert\mu(y)\preceq R^{-\epsilon},$$ with this estimate being uniform in $x$. This proves that $W\in K^\infty(V, \mu)$.\qed
<!-- end head-6 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{griglemma}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph and let $W \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$ have finite support. Then $W$ is Green-bounded on $(V, \mu)$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- head-7: body_md -->
Let $\Omega\subseteq V$ be a finite connected set containing the support of $W$. It suffices to prove separately that $$\sup_{x\in \Omega\cup\partial \Omega}\sum_{y\in V}\left\vertW(y)\right\vert G_\mu(x,y)\mu(y)<+\infty$$ and $$\sup_{x\notin \Omega\cup\partial \Omega}\sum_{y\in V}\left\vertW(y)\right\vert G_\mu(x,y)\mu(y)<+\infty.$$

First note that $\Omega\cup\partial \Omega$ is finite, and since a supremum over a finite set of real numbers is finite, we have $$\sup_{x\in \Omega\cup\partial \Omega}\sum_{y\in V}\left\vertW(y)\right\vert G_\mu(x,y)\mu(y)<+\infty.$$



Next, fix a distinguished point $o\in \Omega$. For $x\notin \Omega\cup \partial \Omega$, the function $u_x(y)=G_\mu(x,y)$ satisfies $\Delta_\mu u_x=0$ on $\Omega$. Therefore by the Harnack inequality of Lemma \ref{localharnackfull}, there exists $C>0$ such that for all $x\notin\Omega\cup\partial \Omega$, $$\sup_\Omega u_x\leq C\inf_\Omega u_x.$$ Hence $G_\mu(x,y)\asymp G_\mu(x, o)$ over all $x\notin \Omega\cup\partial \Omega$ and all $y\in \Omega$. Therefore for $x\notin \Omega\cup \partial \Omega$ we have $$\sum_{y\in V} \left\vertW(y)\right\vert G_\mu(x,y)\mu(y)=\sum_{y\in \Omega} \left\vertW(y)\right\vert G_\mu(x,y)\mu(y)\asymp G_\mu(x, o)\sum_{y\in \Omega} \left\vertW(y)\right\vert\mu(y).$$ By Barlow \cite{barlow1} Theorem 1.31 we have that $G_\mu(x,o)\leq G_\mu(o,o)<+\infty$ for all $x\in V$. Therefore we have that $$\sup_{x\notin \Omega\cup\partial \Omega}\sum_{y\in V}\left\vertW(y)\right\vert G_\mu(x,y)\mu(y) \preceq G_\mu(o,o)\sum_{y\in \Omega} \left\vertW(y)\right\vert\mu(y)<+\infty$$ as desired.\qed
<!-- end head-7 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{smalls}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph and assume that $W$ is Green-bounded on $V$. If $\left\VertW\right\Vert_\mu<\frac{1}{2}$, then $\Delta_\mu+W$ has a profile $h>0$ such that $h\asymp 1$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- head-8: body_md -->
Define a bounded operator $T_W \colon L^\infty(V, d\mu) \rightarrow L^\infty(V, d\mu)$ by $$T_Wf(x)=\sum_{y\in V}W(y)G_\mu(x,y)f(y)\mu(y).$$ Note that $\left\VertT_Wf\right\Vert_\infty\leq \left\VertW\right\Vert_\mu\left\Vertf\right\Vert_\infty$ for all $f\in L^\infty(V, d\mu)$. In particular, if $\left\VertW\right\Vert_\mu<1$, then $I+T_W$ is invertible by a Neumann series: $$(I+T_W)^{-1}=\sum_{k=0}^\infty (-T_W)^k.$$ If $h=(I+T_W)^{-1}1=\sum_{k=0}^\infty (-T_W)^k 1$, then $$\left\verth\right\vert\leq \sum_{k=0}^\infty \left\VertW\right\Vert_\mu^k<+\infty$$ and $$\left\verth\right\vert\geq 1-\sum_{k=1}^\infty \left\VertW\right\Vert_\mu^k=1-\frac{\left\VertW\right\Vert_\mu}{1-\left\VertW\right\Vert_\mu}>0.$$ Thus $h>0$ with $h\asymp 1$. We also have that $$h(x)=1-\sum_{y\in V} W(y)G_\mu(x,y)h(y)\mu(y)$$  which implies $\Delta_\mu h= -Wh$ or $$(\Delta_\mu +W)h=0.$$\qed
<!-- end head-8 -->
<!-- head-9: body_md -->
With $\nu$ defined in terms of $\mu$ and $h$ as above, we write $\nu=h^2\mu$ to denote the new $h$-transformed weights on $V$. This notation has been chosen to mimic that used for $h$-transforms on manifolds, but we caution that this has meaning for not only the vertices but also the edges of the weighted graph.\\
<!-- end head-9 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph and let $W$ be a graph potential on $(V, \mu).$ Let $h>0$ satisfy $(\Delta_\mu+W)h=0$. If $\nu=h^2\mu$, then $(V, \nu)$ is a weighted graph and $$K_\nu(x,y)=\frac{h(y)}{h(x)}K_\mu^W(x,y)$$ for all $x,y\in V$. In particular, $(V, \nu)$ is uniformly lazy and has controlled weights.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- head-10: body_md -->
First we must show that $(V, \nu)$ is uniformly lazy, i.e. there exists $c>0$ such that for all $x\in V,$ $$1-\sum_{y\sim x}\frac{\nu_{xy}}{\nu(x)}\geq c.$$ Since $(\Delta_\mu+W)h=0$ we have that $$h(x)-\left(\sum_{y\simeq x}K_\mu(x,y)h(y)\right)+W(x)h(x)=0.$$

We have $$1-\sum_{y\sim x} \frac{\nu_{xy}}{\nu(x)}=1-\sum_{y\sim x}\frac{h(y)\mu_{xy}}{h(x)\mu(x)}$$ $$=\frac{1}{h(x)}\left(h(x)-\sum_{y\simeq x}K_\mu(x,y)h(y)\right)+K_\mu(x,x)$$ $$=\frac{1}{h(x)}\left(\Delta_\mu h(x)\right)+K_\mu(x,x)=-W(x)+K_\mu(x,x)=K_\mu^W(x,x).$$

Since $W$ is a graph potential, there exists $c>0$ with $-W(x)+K_\mu(x,x)\geq c$. Therefore the weighted graph $(V, \nu)$ is uniformly lazy. The fact that $(V, \nu)$ has controlled weights follows from the Harnack inequality applied to $h$. Namely, if $C_1>0$ such that $h(x)\leq  C_1h(y)$ for all $x\sim y$ and $C_2>0$ is such that $$\frac{\mu_{xy}}{\mu(x)}\geq \frac{1}{C_2}$$ for $x\sim y$, then for $x\sim y$ we have that $$\frac{\nu_{xy}}{\nu(x)}=\frac{h(y)\mu_{xy}}{h(x)\mu(x)}\geq \frac{1}{C_1C_2}.$$ Thus $(V, \nu)$ has controlled weights. Furthermore, we have the identity $$K_\nu(x,y)=\frac{h(y)}{h(x)}K_\mu^W(x,y)$$ which is valid for all $x,y\in V$.\qed
<!-- end head-10 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{classicalh}
With profile $h>0$ for $\Delta_\mu+W$ as above, and weights $\mu=h^2\nu$, we have that for $f \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$, $$\Delta_\nu(f)=\frac{1}{h}(\Delta_\mu+W)(hf)$$ and for any $x,y\in V$, $n\in \mathbf{N}$, $$p_\mu^W(x,y,n)=h(x)h(y)p_\nu(x,y,n).$$
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- head-11: body_md -->
For $f \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$, it is straightforward to verify that $$\Delta_\nu(f)=\frac{1}{h}(\Delta_\mu+W)(hf).$$

Next, a straightforward induction shows that $$K_{\nu, n}(x,y)=\frac{h(y)}{h(x)}K_{\mu, n}^W(x,y)$$ for all $x,y\in V$. Therefore the heat kernel of $\Delta_\nu$ is given by $$p_\nu(x,y,n)=\frac{K_{\nu, n}(x,y)}{\nu(y)}=\frac{p_\mu^W(x,y,n)}{h(x)h(y)}.$$\qed
<!-- end head-11 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{graphpotentials}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph and let $W_1, W_2 \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$ be such that $W_1$ and $W_1+W_2$ are graph potentials on $(V, \mu)$. Let $h>0$ be such that $(\Delta_\mu+W)h=0$ and let $\nu=h^2\mu$. Then $W_2$ is a graph potential on $(V, \nu)$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- head-12: body_md -->
There exists $\epsilon>0$ such that $W_1(x)+W_2(x)\leq K_\mu(x,x)-\epsilon$ for all $x\in V$. We then have that $W_2(x)\leq K_\mu(x,x)-W_1(x)-\epsilon=K_\nu(x,x)-\epsilon$ for all $x\in V$, proving that $W_2$ is a graph potential on $(V, \nu)$.\qed
<!-- end head-12 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{iter} Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph and let $W_1, W_2 \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$ be such that $W_1$ and $W_1+W_2$ are graph potentials on $(V, \mu)$. Let $g,h>0$ be positive functions on $V$ satisfying $(\Delta_\mu+W_1)h=0$ and $(\Delta_\nu+W_2)g=0$, where $\nu=h^2\mu$. Then letting $\theta=g^2h^2\mu$, we have that \begin{equation}
p^{W_1+W_2}_\mu(x,y, n)=g(x)h(x)g(y)h(y)p_\theta(x,y,n)
\end{equation} for all $t>0$ and $x,y\in M$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- head-13: body_md -->
Note that \begin{equation}
(\Delta_\mu+W_1+W_2)(gh)=h\Delta_\nu g+W_2gh=h(\Delta_\nu +W_2)g=0.
\end{equation} Thus $gh$ is a profile for $\Delta_\mu+W_1+W_2$. The conclusion then follows from Lemma \ref{classicalh}.\qed
<!-- end head-13 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{itergreen}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph and let $W_1, W_2 \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$ be such that $W_1$ and $W_1+W_2$ are graph potentials on $(V, \mu)$. Let $h>0$ satsify $(\Delta_\mu+W_1)h=0$ and let $\nu=h^2\mu$. Let $g>0$ satisfy $(\Delta_\nu+W_2)g=0$ and let $\theta=g^2\nu$. Then the following are equivalent:

\noindent(a) $\Delta_\mu+W_1+W_2$ is subcritical.

\noindent(b) $\Delta_\nu+W_2$ is subcritical.

\noindent(c) $(M, \theta, K_\theta)$ is transient.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- head-14: body_md -->
Follows directly from summing Lemma \ref{iter} over $n\in \mathbf{N}$.\qed
<!-- end head-14 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{unique}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a weighted graph satisfying HK($\beta$). Let $W \colon V \rightarrow \mathbf R$ be a graph potential such that $\Delta_\mu+W$ admits a profile $h>0$ with $h\asymp 1$. Let $g>0$ be another profile of $\Delta_\mu+W$. Then $g/h$ is constant.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- head-15: body_md -->
Let $\nu=h^2\mu$. Then $(V, \nu)$ satisfies HK($\beta$) and therefore (EHI). We have that $g/h$ is positive and $\Delta_\nu$-harmonic. By Liouville's theorem, $g/h$ is constant.\qed
<!-- end head-15 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{compactstep}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph satifying HK($\beta$). Let $W$ be a graph potential with finite support such that $\Delta_\mu+tW$ is subcritical for all $0\leq t\leq 1$. Then $\Delta_\mu+W$ has a profile $h$ with $$h\asymp 1.$$
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- head-16: body_md -->
Consider the set $J=\left\{0\leq t\leq 1\colon \Delta_\mu+tW \textrm{ has a profile }h\asymp 1\right\}$. Assume for a contradiction that $[0,1]\setminus J$ is nonempty and let $s=\inf ([0,1]\setminus J).$ By Lemma \ref{smalls}, $s>0$.\\

Let $h>0$ be a profile for $\Delta_\mu+sW$ and let $\nu=h^2\mu$. Since $\Delta_\mu+sW$ is subcritical, by Lemma \ref{itergreen}, $(V, \nu)$ is transient.\\

By Lemma \ref{griglemma}, $W$ is Green-bounded on $(M, \nu)$. Therefore by Lemma \ref{smalls} there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that $s-\epsilon>0$ and $\Delta_\nu-\epsilon W$ has a profile $g>0$ with $g\asymp 1$. It follows that $gh\asymp h$ is a profile for $\Delta_\mu+(s-\epsilon)W$. By Lemma \ref{unique}, $gh\asymp 1$ and therefore $h\asymp 1$, a contradiction. Thus $J=[0,1]$.\qed
<!-- end head-16 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{compactstep2}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph satifying HK($\beta$). Let $W$ be a graph potential with finite support be such that $\Delta_\mu+W$ is subcritical. Then $\Delta_\mu+W$ has a profile $h$ with $$h\asymp 1.$$
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- head-17: body_md -->
Step 1: Assume $W\geq 0$. Here we have that $\Delta_\mu+tW$ is subcritical for all $0\leq t\leq 1$ so Proposition \ref{compactstep} implies the conclusion.\\

Step 2: General case. Here write $W=W_+-W_-$ where $W_+, W_-\geq 0$ are of finite support. Then by Step 1, $\Delta_\mu+W_+$ has a profile $h>0$ with $h\asymp 1$. Let $\nu=h^2\mu$ and consider the graph $(V, \nu, K_\nu)$. Since $(V, \mu, K_\mu)$ satisfies HK($\beta$), so does $(V, \nu, K_\nu)$.\\

Further, $\Delta_\nu-W_-$ is subcritical by Lemma \ref{itergreen}, and in fact since $-tW_-\geq -W_-$ for all $0\leq t\leq 1$, $\Delta_\nu-tW_-$ is subcritical for all $0\leq t\leq 1$. Therefore by Proposition \ref{compactstep}, $\Delta_\nu-W_-$ has a profile $g>0$ with $g\asymp 1$.\\

Finally, $gh\asymp 1$ is a profile for $\Delta_\mu+W$, as desired.\qed
<!-- end head-17 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{maintheorem}
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph satisfying HK($\beta$). Let $W\in K^\infty(V, \mu)$ be a graph potential. If $\Delta_\mu+W$ is subcritical, then there exists a profile $h>0$ for $\Delta_\mu+W$ satisfying $$h\asymp 1.$$
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- head-18: body_md -->
Since $W\in K^\infty(V, \mu)$, we can write $W=W_1+W_2$ where $W_2$ has finite support disjoint from that of $W_1$ and $$\sup_{x\in V}\sum_{y\in V} G_\mu(x,y)\left\vertW_1(y)\right\vert\mu(y)<\frac{1}{2}.$$ We can also take $W_1$ to be a graph potential. By Lemma \ref{smalls}, there exists a profile $g>0$ for $\Delta_\mu+W_1$ with $g\asymp 1$. Let $\nu=g^2 \mu$. Then $(V, \nu)$ satisfies HK($\beta$), and by Lemma \ref{itergreen} $\Delta_\nu+W_2$ is subcritical.\\

Since $W_2$ has finite support, by Lemma \ref{compactstep2}, $\Delta_\nu+W_2$ has a profile $f>0$ with $f\asymp 1$. Therefore $h=gf$ is a profile for $\Delta_\mu+W$ satisfying $h\asymp 1$.\qed
<!-- end head-18 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
Assume that the Schr\"odinger operator $\Delta_\mu+W$ is subcritical with respect to the discrete time random walk. Then $\Delta_\mu+W$ is subcritical with respect to the continuous time random walk.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- head-19: body_md -->
Let $h>0$ be a profile for $\Delta_\mu+W$ and let $\nu=h^2\mu$. From Barlow \cite{barlow1}, $$q_\nu(x,y,t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{e^{-t}t^n}{n!}p_\nu(x,y,n).$$ It follows from Lemma \ref{classicalh} that $$q_\mu^W(x,y,t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{e^{-t}t^n}{n!}p_\mu^W(x,y,n).$$ We therefore have that $$\int_0^\infty q_\mu^W(x,y,t)dt=\sum_{n=0}^\infty p_\mu^W(x,y,n),$$ and the result follows.\qed
<!-- end head-19 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
Let $(V, \mu)$ be a transient weighted graph and assume that $W$ is Green-bounded on $(V, \mu)$. Assume that the Schr\"odinger operator $\Delta_\mu+W$ is subcritical on $(V, \mu)$. Then the Feynman-Kac gauge $h$ is a profile for $\Delta_\mu+W$.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- head-20: body_md -->
Note that for $x\in V$, we have $$\sum_{y\in V}G_\mu(x,y)\left\vertW(y)\right\vert\mu(y)=\sum_{y\in V}\left(\int_0^\infty q_\mu(x,y,t)dt\right) \left\vertW(y)\right\vert\mu(y)$$ $$=\int_0^\infty \sum_{y\in V} q_\mu(x,y,t)\left\vertW(y)\right\vert\mu(y)dt= \int_0^\infty E^x\left[ \left\vertW(Y_t)\right\vert\right]dt=E^x\left[\int_0^\infty \left\vertW(Y_s)\right\vert ds\right].$$ Therefore $\sup_{x\in V} E^x\left[\int_0^\infty \left\vertW(Y_s)\right\vert ds\right]=C<+\infty$. By Jensen's inequality, we have that $$h(x)=E^x\left[\exp\left(-\int_0^\infty W(Y_s)ds\right)\right]\geq \exp\left(-E^x\left[\int_0^\infty W(Y_s)ds\right]\right)\geq e^{-C}>0.$$ Thus $h$ is strictly positive. Furthermore, if $x\in V$ and $\tau\sim \exp(1)$ denotes the first jumping time $\tau=\inf\left\{t\colon N_t>0\right\}$, then by the Markov property, $$h(x)=E^x\left[\exp\left(-\int_0^\infty W(Y_s)ds\right)\right]$$ $$=E^x\left[\exp\left(-\int_0^\tau W(Y_s)ds\right)E^{Y_\tau}\left[\exp\left(-\int_0^\infty W(Y_s)ds\right)\right]\right]$$ $$=E^x\left[\exp\left(-\int_0^\tau W(Y_s)ds\right)h(Y_\tau)\right]=E^x\left[e^{-\tau W(x)}h(Y_\tau)\right].$$ Since $e^{-\tau W(x)}$ and $h(Y_\tau)$ are independent, we have that $$h(x)=E^x\left[e^{-\tau W(x)}h(Y_\tau)\right]=E^x\left[e^{-\tau W(x)}\right]E^x\left[h(Y_\tau)\right]=\frac{1}{1+W(x)}(K_\mu h)(x).$$ We therefore conclude that $$h+Wh=K_\mu h$$ or $$(\Delta_\mu+W)h=0.$$ Thus $h$ is a profile for $\Delta_\mu+W$.\qed
<!-- end head-20 -->
<!-- head-21: body_md -->
By Theorem \ref{maintheorem}, there exists a profile $h>0$ for $\Delta_\mu+W$ satisfying $h\asymp 1$. Let $\nu=h^2\mu$.\\

By Theorem \ref{bassbarlowthm}, the weighted graph $(V, \nu)$ satisfies HK($\beta$). The conclusion then follows from Lemma \ref{classicalh}.\qed
<!-- end head-21 -->

<!-- end example-1 -->
